observations: Three photos show multiple M.2 SATA SSDs laid out side by side.
The SSDs have white labels with barcodes, regulatory marks (CE, FCC), and some visible text.
The brand 'SanDisk' is visible on the labels in photo 0 and photo 1.
The model number 'SDS2210' is visible on the label in photo 0 and photo 1.
The capacity '128GB' is visible on the label in photo 0 and photo 1.
The form factor is M.2, with a SATA interface (indicated by the label and pin layout).
Green circular stickers are placed over some parts of the labels, possibly to obscure serial numbers or other details.
The SSDs appear to be used, with some minor scuffs and wear visible on the circuit boards.
No signs of physical damage such as cracks or bent pins are visible.

claims.evidence: Capacity '128GB' and form factor 'M.2 SATA' are visible on the labels in photo 0 and photo 1.
All visible SSDs in the photos are branded 'SanDisk' with model 'SDS2210'. No other makes are visible.
No test results, logs, or proof of testing are shown in the photos. The claim cannot be verified remotely.

risks.risk: SSD may have hidden wear or bad blocks not visible in photos
risks.proof: A screenshot of SMART data or a test report showing health status and wear level.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially degraded or failing

risks.risk: SSD may have been cloned or repurposed (e.g., from a failed drive)
risks.proof: A video showing the SSD being powered on and recognized by a system, or a test report from a diagnostic tool.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified, possibly counterfeit or repurposed

risks.risk: Serial numbers or other identifying marks may be obscured or altered
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the label without green stickers, showing full serial number and manufacturing details.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially counterfeit or tampered

proof_requests: A close-up photo of the label without green stickers, showing full serial number and manufacturing details.
A screenshot of SMART data or a test report showing health status and wear level.
A video showing the SSD being powered on and recognized by a system.
response.reason: While the SSDs are identifiable as SanDisk SDS2210 128GB M.2 SATA drives, the claim of 'various makes' is contradicted by the photos. The 'fully tested' claim is unverifiable remotely. Hidden risks such as wear, bad blocks, or tampering cannot be ruled out without additional proof. Therefore, further evidence is required before pricing.
